title: Proof pack index (proof-index.json)
description: The machine-readable index of a proof pack, written by the assembler/verifier of workflows/research-proof.js. One entry per claim, in NARRATION ORDER. Designers build the on-screen proof visuals from this file, so every best_visual must be a file someone opened and confirmed. Paths are relative to the proof pack root. Mirrors the README.md tables (templates/proof-pack-README.md).

examples: My video proof pack: verifier index

verified_at.description: When the live re-checks ran (ISO time or range).

order_basis.description: What the order and the approximate times are based on (transcript, word files). Times shift with every cut: say so.

examples.~: partly right; use the honest line

accent.description: How the highlight versions were drawn.

kind.description: narration = the creator says it; context = not said, but a designer may need it (e.g. a release date); supporting = extra evidence for another entry (e.g. a license file behind a README claim).

id.description: Stable id, same as the item id in <folder>/sources.json.

narration_time_approx.description: Approximate time(s) on the current timeline, e.g. "4:10" or "0:17 and 22:01"; "(context)" for context entries.

narration_quote.description: What the creator says (short quote). For context entries: "(not narrated) <what it is>".

status.description: Verdict after the independent re-check. Rounded/temporary variants mean: fine as said, but show the exact source value on screen.

verified_value.description: What the source shows NOW, quoted where possible, with exact figures and the capture time for anything that moves.

best_visual.description: The ONE file to put on screen for this claim (relative path). Prefer a *-highlight.png or *-crop.png that fits a 16:9-ish panel; never a very tall capture.

honest_line.description: For ✗ and ~: a corrected line in the creator's voice that the source supports. null when the claim matches.

suggested_line.description: An on-screen or spoken wording that is safe to use (may be set for ✓ entries too, e.g. rounding a live counter).

verifier_recheck.description: What the independent verifier re-checked live, how, and when.

do_not_show.description: Things visible in the capture that must never reach the screen (third-party names, prices of the creator's own paid community, emails, account details). Designers crop or blur them.

risk.description: Set when the entry must be raised with the creator (e.g. a license or terms clause that contradicts a claim). A flag, not a verdict.
